problems.field: design_class (and the randomized-experiment comparison types ai_vs_bau and ai_design on every S2 contrast)
problems.form_value: online_rct. The same study codes assignment.randomized = not_stated and participants.population = general_public, and the form's agreed_fields_checked entry for this field says confirmed: false.
problems.source_says: Section 6 calls Study 2 a preregistered replication with 640 participants in six conditions. It never says how participants were allocated. It names Prolific only for the 320 student raters, not for the people who wrote the ideas. The codebook defines online_rct as a randomized experiment on an online panel, so the text supports neither part of the code. Codebook section 5 reserves ai_vs_bau and ai_design for randomized experiments, so the S2 contrast types rest on the same inference from Study 1.
problems.quote: To test the robustness of our results and their generalizability to another domain, we conducted a preregistered replication study
problems.locator: p. 10, Section 6.1, first sentence; p. 11, Section 6.1 (raters via Prolific; N = 640 across six conditions); p. 3, Introduction; whole PDF searched for 'random', 'assign', and 'allocat'

confirmed.statement: Study 1 states random assignment of individuals in the Procedure: 'After providing informed consent, participants were randomly assigned to one of the five experimental conditions.' The form's assignment quote is verbatim.

Figure 1 repeats it: 'Participants (N = 486) were randomly assigned to one of five conditions: four LLM variants (vanilla, model-led, suggestion, question) or a control group without support.' The Abstract and the Introduction call Study 1 a randomized controlled experiment, and Section 4 calls it preregistered and gives the AsPredicted link (nf5r-cmrt).
confirmed.locator: p. 2, Figure 1 caption; p. 1, Abstract; p. 3, Introduction; p. 5, Section 4

confirmed.statement: unit = individual and structure = between are right for Study 1. Each participant was assigned to one of five conditions, and the tests use t(481) on 486 people, one row per person.

Check (b): the assignment gave or withheld GPT-4.1 help for the participant's own idea. AI-arm participants 'engaged with the chatbot according to their assigned condition' and submitted their own final idea, which four experts rated. The conditions do not differ only in whose output is rated.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 4.1, third paragraph; p. 6, Section 4.2, first paragraph; p. 7, Section 4.4

confirmed.statement: Check (c): the tool is a large language model. 'all LLM-assisted conditions used GPT-4.1 via the OpenAI API (snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14)', at temperature 0.7 per the Table 5 note. The Table 5 vanilla row says 'Standard GPT-4 model with default behavior', which is also an LLM. The form records this conflict in name_model.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2, first paragraph; p. 19, Appendix A, Table 5 and note

confirmed.statement: Check (d): the comparison arms match the form. The control had no AI ('Participants generated and refined their idea without any LLM support', and Table 5 says 'No AI assistance provided'). The other four arms are GPT-4.1 configurations, so AI-versus-control rows are ai_vs_bau and AI-versus-AI rows are ai_design.
confirmed.locator: p. 7, Section 4.2, Control bullet; p. 19, Table 5; p. 12, Table 3

confirmed.statement: The Figure 1 caption says 'all participants were instructed to refine their idea using the LLM', but Section 4.1 says 'participants either received support in an LLM condition or formulated the idea on their own', and Section 4.2 and Table 5 give the control no AI. The form flags the caption and codes the control ai = none, as the body text supports.
confirmed.locator: p. 2, Figure 1 caption, part B; p. 5, Section 4.1, third paragraph; p. 7, Control bullet; p. 19, Table 5

confirmed.statement: The Study 1 arm descriptions match Section 4.2 and Table 5: model-led (initial idea of at most 10 words, one-shot rewrite of at most 40 words, optional refinement), suggestion-mode (three alternatives, then three elaboration suggestions), and vanilla (same chat interface, no system prompt, free chat). The question-mode description follows the Table 5 prompt and the Figure 2 screenshot, where the LLM asks the user to 'propose an alternative idea'. The form notes that Section 4.2 instead says 'The LLM generated three alternative ideas'.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2 and Figure 2; p. 7, Vanilla bullet; p. 19, Table 5

confirmed.statement: how_used codes model-led as refinement. The paper calls it 'model-led idea refinement' and says LLMs 'proactively refined participants' ideas', although Section 4.2 says the 10-word cap made the model perform 'the primary creative elaboration rather than merely refining an already developed idea'. Either reading is an AI rewrite of the participant's own draft, and the study-level role stays other.
confirmed.locator: p. 3, Introduction and contribution (1); p. 6, Section 4.2, Model-led bullet

confirmed.statement: arms[].n_analyzed (96, 95, 101, 95, 99) match Table 2 and sum to 486. The paper prints no per-arm counts at assignment, so arms[].n_randomized = null is right. participants.n_randomized = null is defensible, because Section 4 gives N = 502 for the randomized experiment while Figure 1 says N = 486 were randomly assigned.
confirmed.locator: p. 12, Table 2; p. 7, Section 4.3; p. 5, Section 4; p. 2, Figure 1

confirmed.statement: Check (e): the only within-person comparison (S1-O3, initial idea vs refined idea) has a fixed order. Participants in the model-led and human-led arms wrote the initial idea without AI before the AI interaction. The form codes these rows before_after, says they are not randomized contrasts, and does not use them for criterion 1.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2, first paragraph; p. 8, Section 5.3; p. 10, Figure 5

confirmed.statement: Study 2 assignment.randomized = not_stated is right. Every 'random' in the PDF concerns Study 1, the 20-conversation coding subset, random effects, or a reference title. The form's Study 2 quote and preregistration link (aspredicted.org/de6md8) are on p. 10.

Study 2 arms match Table 4 and Section 6: six conditions, including a model-led iterative arm and a control 'without LLM support'. All AI conditions used GPT-4.1 at temperature 0.7. The vanilla description ('without system prompt') follows Study 1's definition and Table 6, which lists prompts for each adapted condition and none for vanilla.
confirmed.locator: p. 12, Table 4; p. 13, Section 6.3; pp. 10-11, Section 6.1; p. 20, Appendix A, Table 6 and note

confirmed.statement: Criterion 1 holds on Study 1 alone: individuals were randomly assigned to four GPT-4.1 conditions or a no-LLM control on an adapted Alternative Uses Test, and 486 people were analyzed.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 4.1; p. 7, Sections 4.2 and 4.3; p. 12, Table 2

summary: The PDF confirms that Study 1 randomly assigned individuals, after consent, to one of four GPT-4.1 conditions or a no-LLM control on an adapted Alternative Uses Test (p. 5, Section 4.1; p. 2, Figure 1), and the form's arms, tool, comparison arms, and fixed-order within-person rows all match the text. The one unsupported code is Study 2's design_class online_rct, because the paper never states how Study 2 allocated participants or where it recruited them, but criterion 1 holds on Study 1 alone.
